# Changelog

 This page includes release notes and updates for Jira Cloud app developers. Use this page to keep track of upcoming changes, deprecation notices, new features, and feature updates from Jira Cloud Platform.

# Forge changelog

For updates about changes to the Forge platform, see the [Forge changelog](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/changelog/) in the Forge documentation.

Go to our [developer community](https://community.developer.atlassian.com/c/Jira/) to ask questions. You may also be interested in the [*What's New blog* for Atlassian Cloud](https://confluence.atlassian.com/cloud/blog) where details of major changes that affect all users of the Jira Cloud products are announced.

## 23 November 2026

#### Added RichDocument type in Jira expressions

We've released support for a [RichDocument](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference/#richdocument) type in Jira expressions, based on [RFC-150](https://community.developer.atlassian.com/t/rfc-150-jira-expression-enhancements-for-rich-text-fields/103048/1).

Rich text fields can hold content as ADF or as wiki markup, depending on the field and how its value was saved. Until now, expressions had to handle each format themselves. RichDocument.of(value) accepts any of them, so you can ask questions about the content or read it in another format without checking how it was stored.

RichDocument provides:

- `isEmpty()`: the field holds no content as a `Boolean`
- `isBlank()`: the field holds nothing a reader would see as a `Boolean`.
- `asPlainText()`: the content as a `PlainText`.
- `asWikiText()`: the content as a `WikiText`.
- `asAdfMap()`: the content as an ADF `Map`.

[PlainText](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference/#plaintext) and [WikiText](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference/#wikitext) also provide `contains(text)`, `getPrefix(maxLength)` and `toString()` functions. PlainText answers about the text a reader sees. WikiText answers about the wiki markup, syntax included.

##### More details

[RichDocument](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference/#richdocument) can be used anywhere Jira expressions are evaluated. Below are a few common places, with an example for each.

**Workflow validators**

Require a rich text field before a transition and tell the user what's missing:

`1 2``let impact = RichDocument.of(issue.customfield_10797); impact.isBlank() ? 'Please describe the impact.' : true`

**Workflow conditions**

Only offer a transition, such as Approve, to someone mentioned in a comment:

`1 2 3``let bodies = issue.comments.map(c => RichDocument.of(c.body)); bodies.some(body => body.asPlainText().contains('@[' + user.accountId + ']'))`

**Transforming search results with the REST API**

Give the [evaluate Jira expression](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-jira-expressions/#api-rest-api-3-expression-eval-post) operation a JQL query, and use an expression to choose what comes back for each matching issue. This example returns a plain-text excerpt instead of the full document:

`1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8``issues.map(i => { let description = RichDocument.of(i.description); return { key: i.key, excerpt: description.asPlainText().getPrefix(200), hasDescription: !description.isBlank() }; })`

The same operation is a quick way to try out an expression before using it in a module.

## 20 November 2026

#### Added Forge Jira global pages now support anonymous and unlicensed user access

**What's changing**
Forge apps can now enable anonymous and unlicensed users to access the Jira global page module (`jira:globalPage`). This update allows you to provide global-page experiences for users who are not signed in or do not have a Jira product license, including any child pages configured under the global page.

Access remains subject to the site’s access settings and the permissions applicable to the data and APIs used by the app. Enabling this configuration does not grant additional Jira permissions. Existing apps do not need to change unless you want to enable anonymous or unlicensed access.

**What you need to do**
To allow anonymous or unlicensed users to access your global page, add the `unlicensedAccess` property to the `jira:globalPage` module in your `manifest.yml` file:

`1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9``modules: jira:globalPage: - key: my-global-page resource: main resolver: function: resolver unlicensedAccess: - anonymous - unlicensed`

For more information, see the [Jira global page module reference](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-global-page/) and the guide on [Access to Forge apps for unlicensed users](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/access-to-forge-apps-for-unlicensed-users/).

## 13 November 2026

#### Announcement Jira Cloud REST APIs: HTTP 422 response when configuration limits are exceeded

We are extending enforcement of Jira Cloud configuration limits to additional REST API operations. This aligns REST API behavior with the limits enforced through Jira’s administration experience and helps protect site performance and reliability. [https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/data-limits-and-guardrails/](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/data-limits-and-guardrails/)

**What is changing?**

Affected REST API operations will return **HTTP** `422 Unprocessable Entity` when a request would exceed the applicable configuration limit. This includes attempts to add configuration entries when the relevant scope has already reached or exceeded its limit.

**This introduces limit enforcement, not just a status-code change for requests that already failed. Some requests that previously succeeded will now be rejected with HTTP** `422` when the enforcement applies.

The OpenAPI specifications for the affected endpoints have been updated to document this response.

**Action required**

Developers maintaining apps, integrations, scripts, or automation that use these endpoints should:

- Update error handling to recognize HTTP `422` as a possible response for configuration-limit violations.
- Inspect the response body to identify the configuration-limit violation and provide administrators with guidance for resolving it.
- Avoid automatically retrying the same request without addressing the underlying limit. Reduce configuration usage or adjust the operation so it stays within the applicable limit before retrying.

**Affected endpoints**

**Rollout**

We plan to begin rolling out this change on **11–12 November 2026 as the planned rollout-start window**. Once enabled for a site, affected Jira Cloud platform REST API operations will return **HTTP** `422 Unprocessable Entity` when a request would exceed an applicable configuration limit.

## 12 November 2026

#### Announcement New Ecoscanner Security Checks Coming Soon for Marketplace Forge Apps

**What’s Changing**

We're expanding Ecoscanner with new automated security checks for Marketplace Forge apps to ensure compliance with our [Security Requirements for Cloud Apps](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/marketplace/security-requirements/). These checks will be released periodically before **December 31, 2026**.

The new checks include:

- **Arbitrary code execution**: Detects untrusted input reaching dynamic code execution (e.g., `eval`) in Forge functions (Requirement 8, Critical Severity).
- **End-of-life Node.js runtimes**: Flags apps using Node.js runtimes that have reached end-of-life (Requirement 10, Critical Severity).
- **Atlassian API token usage**: Detects apps authenticating to Atlassian APIs using user API tokens instead of app-based authentication (Requirement 11, Critical Severity).
- **Secrets in logs**: Detects sensitive data (e.g., credentials) written to application logs via `console.log` or similar (Requirement 5, High Severity).
- **SQL injection**: Detects user input interpolated directly into Forge SQL queries instead of using query parameters (Requirement 8, High Severity).
- **TLS and HSTS on Forge remotes**: Verifies that remote backends accept only TLS 1.2+ and return an HSTS header with a `max-age` of at least one year (Requirement 3, Medium Severity).

**What You Need to Do**

As these scanners go live, findings will be reported to you via AMS tickets in [ecosystem.atlassian.net](https://ecosystem.atlassian.net/jira/for-you).

To account for the holiday period, we are providing an additional 30 days beyond the standard [Security Bug Fix Policy](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/marketplace/security-bugfix-policy/) for findings from High or Medium severity checks during this initial launch. Standard resolution timeframes will apply to all findings starting **January 1, 2027**.

More details on how these checks work will be included in the [Ecoscanner documentation](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/marketplace/ecoscanner/) as they are released. If you have questions, please contact [Developer Support](https://developer.atlassian.com/support).

## 9 November 2026

#### Announcement Extension of deprecation: Custom field context default value REST APIs

The [custom field context default value REST APIs deprecation](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/changelog/#CHANGE-3082) has been extended to July 2027. This extension provides additional time to migrate as we adjust the timelines for supporting multiple default values per context.

**Updated deprecation timeline:**

- **November 4 2026:** New `GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValues` endpoint available for testing.
- **November-December 2026:** Early access begins for multiple default values per context and the new `PUT /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValues` REST API. You can sign up for early access via [this form](https://privacy.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3769).
- **January 2027:** GA launch of multiple default values per context and the new `PUT /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValues` REST API.
- **July 2027:** The existing (deprecated) default values APIs will be removed.

#### Added Enable pre-rendering for Forge custom field formatter output on Jira issue view

**What's changing**
You can now use the `view.formatter.allowPrerender` manifest property to display a Forge custom field's formatter output as pre-rendered content on the Jira issue view. This content is shown while the field's custom read view is loading, providing a faster and more seamless experience for users.

- **Automatic pre-rendering**: Fields without a custom issue-view renderer are pre-rendered by default.
- **Opt-in pre-rendering**: Fields that use a `view.function` or `view.resource` renderer can now opt in by setting `allowPrerender: true` in the manifest.

**What you need to do**
To enable pre-rendering for your custom field, update your `manifest.yml` file:

1. Locate your `jira:customFieldType` module.
2. Under the `view.formatter` property, add `allowPrerender: true`.

`1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8``modules: jira:customFieldType: - key: my-custom-field name: My Custom Field view: resource: main formatter: allowPrerender: true`

For more details on implementation, see the [Pre-rendering formatter output on Jira issue view](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field-type/#pre-rendering-formatter-output-on-jira-issue-view) documentation.

## 27 October 2026

#### Announcement Descendant search in JQL using portfolioChildIssuesOf() will include team-managed space hierarchies

Starting **February 1, 2027**, we'll progressively roll out a change to the `portfolioChildIssuesOf()` JQL function so its results include work items in team-managed spaces. Today, the function only follows hierarchy in company-managed spaces, so searches can miss descendants that live in team-managed spaces.

### What's changing

- `portfolioChildIssuesOf()` will return descendants through valid team-managed space hierarchies, including supported relationships between company-managed and team-managed spaces, such as a team-managed epic under a company-managed initiative.
- Queries that use `NOT IN portfolioChildIssuesOf()` will exclude these additional work items.
- Results continue to respect hierarchy rules, user permissions and issue security.
- REST API request and response formats don't change.

### What you need to do

If your app, saved filters or automation rules assume that team-managed work items are excluded from `portfolioChildIssuesOf()` results:

1. Find the queries that use `portfolioChildIssuesOf()`.
2. Check whether team-managed work items in the results would affect your logic.
3. If they would, update your queries or result handling before **February 1, 2027**.

We'll publish another update when the rollout starts.

## 26 October 2026

#### Deprecation Notice The Forge CLI now requires Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1 or newer

**What's changing**
We've updated the minimum compatible Node.js version for the Forge CLI. The CLI now requires Node.js **22.23.4**, **24.22.1**, **26.12.1**, or newer.

Node.js 20 has reached end of life and is no longer supported. To continue using the Forge CLI to develop and deploy your apps, you must upgrade your local development environment to one of the supported versions listed above.

**What you need to do**

1. Check your current Node.js version by running `node -v` in your terminal.
2. If you are running a version older than the requirements, download and install a supported version from the [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org).
3. Update your Forge CLI to the latest version by running:npm install -g @forge/cli@latest
4. Verify the installation by running `forge --version`.

For more information on setting up your development environment, see the [Getting started guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/getting-started-learn/#set-up-node-js).

## 16 October 2026

#### Announcement Atlassian cloud will start using new IP address ranges as we expand our cloud infrastructure

**What's changing**
From **January 1, 2027**, Atlassian cloud will add new IP address ranges as we expand our cloud infrastructure.

The new ranges are in addition to our existing ones.

The new ranges are:

- **New range:** `131.162.88.0/21`
  - **Requests to Atlassian** (browsers and your clients calling Atlassian APIs): `131.162.88.0/23`
  - **Requests from Atlassian** (webhooks, Connect lifecycle calls, and other requests from Atlassian to your app): `131.162.90.0/23`

**What you need to do**
If your app, remote backend, or integration allowlists Atlassian IP addresses, you must add these ranges before **January 1, 2027**, to avoid service interruptions.

These ranges are already included in our [official IP range list](https://ip-ranges.atlassian.com) ([viewer tool](https://ip-ranges.atlassian.com/tool.html)). If you automate your allowlist updates from this file, no further action is required. For more details, see our documentation on [IP addresses and domains for Atlassian cloud apps](https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/ip-addresses-and-domains-for-atlassian-cloud-products/).

## 15 October 2026

#### Added (Experimental) New REST APIs for managing and applying space policies in Jira Cloud

**What's changing**
We've introduced new experimental REST APIs for managing space policies in Jira Cloud. Space policies allow site administrators to govern the creation and usage of fields and statuses in team-managed spaces, helping to prevent configuration sprawl and maintain instance health.

The following experimental endpoints are now available:

**Viewing policies**

- `GET /rest/api/3/policies` — Get all policies
- `GET /rest/api/3/policies/project/{projectIdOrKey}` — Get project policy state
- `GET /rest/api/3/policies/project/{projectIdOrKey}/rules` — Get project policy rules

**Applying policies to projects**

- `POST /rest/api/3/policies/{policyId}/apply` — Apply a policy to projects
- `POST /rest/api/3/policies/{policyId}/remove` — Remove a policy from projects
- `PUT /rest/api/3/policies/project/{projectIdOrKey}/policies` — Set the policies applied to a project
- `POST /rest/api/3/policies/project/{projectIdOrKey}/validate` — Validate policy application to a project

**What you need to do**

1. Review the [Jira Cloud space policy API documentation](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-policies/) to understand the available methods and data structures.
2. Note that these APIs are currently **experimental** and may change without notice.
3. If you are building integrations that create fields or statuses, ensure you handle potential blocks when a space policy is active.

## 12 October 2026

#### Added Dynamic modules, customer-managed egress, and customer-managed remotes are now generally available in Forge

Dynamic modules, customer-managed egress, and customer-managed remotes are now generally available on the Forge platform.

- Dynamic modules let a Forge app register and manage modules at runtime through the Dynamic Modules API, rather than declaring them statically in the manifest. These modules are available across Jira, Confluence, and Jira Service Management.
- Customer-managed egress lets Atlassian administrators configure the external domains a Forge app may send data to.
- Customer-managed remotes let Atlassian administrators configure the remote backends a Forge app may communicate with.

For more information, see [Dynamic modules](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/apis-reference/dynamic-modules/) and [Customer-managed egress and remotes](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/customer-managed-egress-and-remotes/).

## 9 October 2026

#### Added Forge display conditions now support arrays under logical operators for Jira and JSM modules

**What's changing**
Forge display conditions for Jira and Jira Service Management (JSM) modules now support arrays under the `and`, `or`, and `not` logical operators.

Previously, manifest keys had to be unique at each level, which made it difficult to repeat the same condition type or group multiple logical expressions. With this update, you can use an array of condition objects to define complex visibility logic more easily.

For example, you can now structure your manifest to group conditions or repeat the same condition type:

`1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8``displayConditions: or: - and: - entityPropertyExists: { entity: user, propertyKey: a } - entityPropertyExists: { entity: user, propertyKey: b } - and: - entityPropertyExists: { entity: user, propertyKey: c } - entityPropertyExists: { entity: user, propertyKey: d }`

**What you need to do**
No action is required for existing apps, as the previous syntax remains supported. If you want to simplify complex logic or repeat conditions in your Jira or JSM modules, you can update your manifest to use the new array-based syntax.

For more details and examples, see the [Forge display conditions documentation](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/display-conditions/#use-the-same-condition-more-than-once--jira-and-jira-service-management-).

## 8 October 2026

#### Announcement Direct JQL validation for custom JQL functions returns to Search REST APIs

We are reintroducing direct JQL query validation to the Search REST API (`/rest/api/3/search/jql`) specifically for queries that use custom JQL functions.

Previously, when the new Search REST API was introduced, JQL validation was moved exclusively to the parse endpoint (`/rest/api/3/jql/parse`). Based on developer feedback, we are bringing this capability back to the search endpoint for custom JQL functions.

If a JQL query containing custom JQL functions is invalid, malformed, or references unsupported functions or arguments, the search API will now return an immediate **HTTP 400 Bad Request** with detailed error messages. This change applies exclusively to custom JQL functions; native JQL queries and other general usages of the search endpoint remain unaffected and will continue to follow existing validation behaviors.

**What you need to do**

1. **Simplify your integration**: If your app uses custom JQL functions, you no longer need to make a separate pre-flight call to the JQL parse API (`/rest/api/3/jql/parse`) to validate these queries before searching.
2. **Update error handling**: Ensure your search API integrations are prepared to handle **HTTP 400 Bad Request** responses and can inspect the returned error messages when executing queries that include custom JQL functions.
3. **Review documentation**: For more information on constructing queries, refer to the [Jira Search REST API documentation](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-search/#api-rest-api-3-search-jql-get).
